statement.p: Find an equation of the plane through the three points given:

static.solution:
\mathbf{n}\cdot \left\lt x,y,z\right>=d
To find the normal vector to the plane, \mathbf{n}, we first compute the vectors \vec{PQ} and \vec{PR} that lie in the plane, and then find the cross product of these vectors. This gives:
\vec{PQ}= \left\lt 6,4,4\right> - \left\lt 3,0,0\right> = \left\lt 3,4,4\right>
\vec{PR}= \left\lt 7,1,-4\right> - \left\lt 3,0,0\right> = \left\lt 4,1,-4\right>
\mathbf{n} = \vec{PQ}\times \vec{PR} = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} \boldsymbol{i} \amp \boldsymbol{j} \amp \boldsymbol{k} \\ 3 \amp 4 \amp 4 \\ 4 \amp 1 \amp -4 \end{array} \right|
\qquad = \left| \begin{array}{cc} 4 \amp 4 \\ 1 \amp -4 \end{array} \right| \boldsymbol{i} -\left| \begin{array}{cc} 3 \amp 4 \\ 4 \amp -4 \end{array} \right| \boldsymbol{j} +\left| \begin{array}{cc} 3 \amp 4 \\ 4 \amp 1 \end{array} \right| \boldsymbol{k}
\qquad =-20 \boldsymbol{i} + 28 \boldsymbol{j} - 13 \boldsymbol{k}
We now choose any of the three points in the plane, say P=\left(3,0,0\right), and compute d.
d=\mathbf{n} \cdot\vec{OP}=\left\lt -20,28,-13\right> \cdot \left\lt 3,0,0\right> = -60
Finally we obtain the following equation of the plane:
-20 x + 28 y - 13 z = -60.
